external_comparison.old_verdict: pedagogically gold-standard with off-topic playground and redaction issues
external_comparison.current_adversarial_conclusion: The old audit did not execute the level-closing validators or propagate known S27-S38 debt. Runtime counterexamples show release, packet, decision, value and CF-3 gates can false-green invalid evidence.

research_basis.use: Risk management is continuous over lifecycle; GOVERN/MAP/MEASURE/MANAGE are outcomes/actions, not a simple one-time checklist.
Fairness assessment uses harm/context-driven disaggregated metrics; MetricFrame requires y_true/y_pred and sensitive features and can report subgroup metrics/support/CI.
SemVer requires a declared public API; MAJOR/MINOR/PATCH have specific compatibility semantics and dotted text alone is not SemVer validation.
SSRF prevention depends on explicit URL/network policy such as allowlists when feasible, not an input_limits boolean.
Human oversight, TEVV, benchmarks, costs and targeted scope should be defined and documented.
Model cards are substantive reporting artifacts, not merely a type name.
Dataset documentation is purposeful, transparent and audience-aware; a 'data' string does not instantiate the artifact.

rejected_findings.claim: S39 should automatically promote the learner because it is the level integrator.
rejected_findings.evidence: The source explicitly says promotion is external and must not be self-declared.

rejected_findings.claim: Using SemVer for internal model/data artifacts is inherently wrong.
rejected_findings.evidence: A project may adopt SemVer-like compatibility contracts; the defect is calling arbitrary dotted strings semver without declared API/compatibility semantics.

rejected_findings.claim: A score should never be used to prioritize human review.
rejected_findings.evidence: Queue prioritization is a legitimate decision-support use when separated from guilt/fraud labels and governed by capacity/uncertainty.

rejected_findings.claim: Human override is conceptually unsafe because it can differ from the model.
rejected_findings.evidence: Human override is a valid control; the defect is missing action validation and audit provenance.

rejected_findings.claim: A checklist has no place in responsible-AI governance.
rejected_findings.evidence: Checklists can be useful indexes; the defect is treating booleans as evidence and collapsing ongoing risk management to one pass/fail.
Input drift is a useful signal; the defect is presenting it as the general mechanism for detecting model degradation.

rejected_findings.claim: The S39-triage-stages figure is necessarily wrong because it emphasizes leakage.
rejected_findings.evidence: The leakage message is valid; the concrete problem is that the alt text omits the model stage from the canonical pipeline.

rejected_findings.claim: Legacy id integrator-phase2 should be renamed now.
rejected_findings.evidence: The source documents it as a stable URL/save key; the fix should target the off-topic playground mapping, not rename the id without migration.

findings.summary: S39 closes N3/CF-3 while S27-S38 remain REPAIR_REQUIRED; upstream evidence cannot be treated as green.
findings.evidence: S39 says it receives CP-N3-A/B/C plus regression S27-S39 and CF-3, while the continuation ledger records unresolved material debt through S38.
findings.pedagogical_impact: A capstone can launder known defects into a false level promotion.
findings.attack: A capstone can launder known defects into a false level promotion.
findings.defense: An integrator should aggregate prior work rather than reteach every dependency.
findings.proposed_fix: Make every upstream gate a machine-readable dependency and block CF-3 on any open critical regression.

findings.summary: S39 declares nine learning outcomes although the roadmap contract specifies exactly eight outcomes per section.
findings.evidence: learningOutcomes contains 9 entries; the roadmap says each section locks ocho resultados observables.
findings.pedagogical_impact: Blueprint drift weakens assessment mapping and equivalence at the level-closing section.
findings.attack: Blueprint drift weakens assessment mapping and equivalence at the level-closing section.
findings.defense: The ninth outcome is substantively relevant to CF-3.
findings.proposed_fix: Merge CF-3 documentation into an existing outcome or revise the authoritative roadmap explicitly.

findings.summary: section_contract() prints policy booleans and gate names rather than evaluating any gate.
findings.evidence: It returns gates=['CP-N3-C','regression_S27_S39','CF-3_external_review'], auto_fraud=False and self_declared_promotion=False.
findings.pedagogical_impact: Learners can mistake declared strings/booleans for evidence that promotion controls exist.
findings.attack: Learners can mistake declared strings/booleans for evidence that promotion controls exist.
findings.defense: The function is clearly a map/reference artifact.
findings.proposed_fix: Rename it manifest_template or connect it to actual test results, artifact hashes and external-review status.

findings.summary: The canonical pipeline is represented as an ordered list of stage names, not an executed end-to-end flow.
findings.evidence: build_pipeline_payload() returns six stage strings and metadata only.
findings.pedagogical_impact: The gate promises integrated triage, but stage ordering alone cannot detect broken interfaces, data loss or routing changes.
findings.attack: The gate promises integrated triage, but stage ordering alone cannot detect broken interfaces, data loss or routing changes.
findings.defense: A declarative stage map is useful orientation.
findings.proposed_fix: Execute a synthetic case through real stage interfaces and assert each contract plus final identity/routing.

findings.summary: build_pipeline_payload() accepts empty case IDs and invalid/non-finite scores.
findings.evidence: No validation is performed on case_id or score.
findings.pedagogical_impact: Corrupt score telemetry can enter the level-closing queue artifact.
findings.attack: Corrupt score telemetry can enter the level-closing queue artifact.
findings.defense: The happy fixture is valid.
findings.proposed_fix: Require stable nonempty case_id and finite score in the declared score domain.

findings.summary: label_space='needs_review' and auto_fraud=False are hard-coded metadata, not controls over downstream behavior.
findings.evidence: The payload always prints auto_fraud False regardless of consumer behavior.
findings.pedagogical_impact: The curriculum can claim no-auto-fraud while no executable guard prevents unsafe mapping.
findings.attack: The curriculum can claim no-auto-fraud while no executable guard prevents unsafe mapping.
findings.defense: The prose repeatedly states the intended safety boundary.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a policy validator/test that rejects forbidden label/action mappings across downstream queue outputs.

findings.summary: The S39-triage-stages figure alt text describes five stages and omits the model stage from the six-stage canonical pipeline.
findings.evidence: Alt says 'Cinco etapas —intake, ER, grafo, features, cola—'; code includes model_score.
findings.pedagogical_impact: The visual model erases a boundary the text says must be versioned and governed.
findings.attack: The visual model erases a boundary the text says must be versioned and governed.
findings.defense: The caption focuses on leakage rather than stage count.
findings.proposed_fix: Show all six stages or explicitly state what is collapsed.

findings.summary: The registry labels versions 'semver' merely when every string contains a dot.
findings.evidence: compat='semver' if all('.' in meta['ver'] ...); 'not.a.version' passes.
findings.pedagogical_impact: Invalid version metadata can satisfy a compatibility concept.
findings.attack: Invalid version metadata can satisfy a compatibility concept.
findings.defense: The lesson is emphasizing intent rather than parser implementation.
findings.proposed_fix: Parse SemVer 2.0.0 and define the public contract/API whose compatibility the version communicates.

findings.summary: The registry omits artifacts the prose says must be owned/versioned: threshold and packet template.
findings.evidence: Prose lists ER engine, graph_schema, feature_set, ranker, threshold and packet template; code registers only four.
findings.pedagogical_impact: Critical decision/explanation artifacts can remain unowned while registry appears complete.
findings.attack: Critical decision/explanation artifacts can remain unowned while registry appears complete.
findings.defense: Four examples illustrate the pattern.
findings.proposed_fix: Test registry completeness against an explicit required-artifact list.

findings.summary: Owner strings are counted but not validated as contactable owners or signers.
findings.evidence: owner_count() counts arbitrary strings and does not resolve contactability/review authority.
findings.pedagogical_impact: Governance ownership becomes decorative metadata rather than escalation.
findings.attack: Governance ownership becomes decorative metadata rather than escalation.
findings.defense: A full identity system is outside the small lab.
findings.proposed_fix: Use a synthetic owner directory with stable IDs/contact route plus release signer fields.

findings.summary: packet_ok() omits uncertainty and model contribution although T2-A says the packet contains those explanation layers.
findings.evidence: need=('case_id','score','evidence','graph_path').
findings.pedagogical_impact: A packet can pass while missing layers that supposedly make it defensible.
findings.attack: A packet can pass while missing layers that supposedly make it defensible.
findings.defense: The prose makes model_contrib optional in one sentence.
findings.proposed_fix: Declare required vs conditional layers explicitly and make the validator match.

findings.summary: packet_ok() rejects score 0.0 but accepts NaN and score 2.0.
findings.evidence: Runtime: 0.0→False; NaN→True; 2.0→True.
findings.pedagogical_impact: Malformed evidence can pass while a legitimate low score fails.
findings.attack: Malformed evidence can pass while a legitimate low score fails.
findings.defense: Truthiness is compact for the happy path.
findings.proposed_fix: Separate key presence from value-domain validation; require finite score in domain.

findings.summary: The packet's evidence list contains derived feature-like labels instead of source evidence records.
findings.evidence: evidence=['shared_phone_synth','tx_path_len_2'].
findings.pedagogical_impact: S35's feature-vs-observed-evidence misconception is carried into CF-3.
findings.attack: S35's feature-vs-observed-evidence misconception is carried into CF-3.
findings.defense: Synthetic labels are easy to read.
findings.proposed_fix: Use immutable evidence IDs/source facts; keep derived features in a separate section.

findings.summary: graph_path is only node labels, with no edge IDs, source records, timestamps or graph snapshot/version.
findings.evidence: ['E1','ph:900','E2'] is treated as path evidence.
findings.pedagogical_impact: The reviewer cannot reconstruct whether the path existed in the model's graph version.
findings.attack: The reviewer cannot reconstruct whether the path existed in the model's graph version.
findings.defense: A node sequence is a useful visual shorthand.
findings.proposed_fix: Add edge/evidence refs, graph snapshot/version and as-of time.

findings.summary: uncertainty='in_distribution' is hand-entered rather than produced by a validated uncertainty/OOD artifact.
findings.evidence: The packet hard-codes in_distribution.
findings.pedagogical_impact: Known S35/S36 uncertainty defects can be laundered into the capstone.
findings.attack: Known S35/S36 uncertainty defects can be laundered into the capstone.
findings.defense: S39 is intended to integrate prior lessons.
findings.proposed_fix: Require uncertainty method/version/reference snapshot/value/status and validation provenance.

findings.summary: model_contrib={'shared_phone':0.4} is not linked to the actual model run, prediction or transformed row.
findings.evidence: No model_run_id, explanation_id or fidelity check appears.
findings.pedagogical_impact: The packet can show an explanation unrelated to its score.
findings.attack: The packet can show an explanation unrelated to its score.
findings.defense: S35 is supposed to provide the semantics.
findings.proposed_fix: Bind explanation to model run, transformed feature lineage and prediction/fidelity.

findings.summary: priority_bucket() accepts NaN/out-of-range scores and invalid threshold ordering.
findings.evidence: Runtime: NaN→skip; thr_hi=.4/thr_lo=.75 with score=.5→queue_now.
findings.pedagogical_impact: Invalid inputs silently become operational decisions.
findings.attack: Invalid inputs silently become operational decisions.
findings.defense: The supplied thresholds are valid.
findings.proposed_fix: Validate finite score and ordered thresholds in the declared domain; fail closed.

findings.summary: The prose says thresholds are selected in validation by capacity/cost, but code uses hand-entered 0.75/0.40.
findings.evidence: No validation dataset, cost function, search or threshold artifact is referenced.
findings.pedagogical_impact: An arbitrary cut can be narrated as validated.
findings.attack: An arbitrary cut can be narrated as validated.
findings.defense: Fixed values keep the example readable.
findings.proposed_fix: Load threshold/version from a validation artifact with objective and capacity assumptions.

findings.summary: queue_load() counts only new queue_now cases and ignores backlog, queue_batch, service rate and horizon.
findings.evidence: within_capacity = n_now <= capacity.
findings.pedagogical_impact: One batch count can be mistaken for operational queue feasibility.
findings.attack: One batch count can be mistaken for operational queue feasibility.
findings.defense: The code calls it a micro-check.
findings.proposed_fix: Rename it accordingly or model backlog/service capacity over a stated shift.

findings.summary: decisions.py contradicts its own prose by omitting actor, reason and timestamp.
findings.evidence: Entries contain case_id, auto, final, override only.
findings.pedagogical_impact: Human override cannot be reconstructed or defended.
findings.attack: Human override cannot be reconstructed or defended.
findings.defense: The code keeps the example short.
findings.proposed_fix: Persist actor_id, reason, occurred_at, policy/model versions and immutable event_id.

findings.summary: Any truthy human string becomes final, including 'fraud'; empty string yields auto while override=True.
findings.evidence: Runtime human='fraud'→fraud; human=''→queue with override True.
findings.pedagogical_impact: Human control can create forbidden labels and inconsistent audit state.
findings.attack: Human control can create forbidden labels and inconsistent audit state.
findings.defense: Human override should beat auto within an allowed action space.
findings.proposed_fix: Validate an allowlisted action enum and explicit override semantics.

findings.summary: The audit log is a process-local list.
findings.evidence: log=[] at module scope.
findings.pedagogical_impact: Restart loses evidence needed for appeal and external review.
findings.attack: Restart loses evidence needed for appeal and external review.
findings.defense: A list demonstrates accumulation.
findings.proposed_fix: Use append-only persistent storage with event IDs and reopen tests.

findings.summary: The section promises appeal with another reviewer, but no appeal object/state/reviewer-separation check exists.
findings.evidence: Appeal exists only in prose.
findings.pedagogical_impact: A governance outcome is unearned.
findings.attack: A governance outcome is unearned.
findings.defense: Conceptual explanation is useful.
findings.proposed_fix: Add appeal request, prior-decision ref, second-reviewer rule, lifecycle and audit events.

findings.summary: The outcome promises feedback operation, yet there is no feedback capture or training-handoff artifact.
findings.evidence: Only a prose warning about temporal leakage exists.
findings.pedagogical_impact: Leakage and verification bias remain untested at the integrator gate.
findings.attack: Leakage and verification bias remain untested at the integrator gate.
findings.defense: The warning itself is correct.
findings.proposed_fix: Create versioned feedback events with label source/time/eligibility and future-training cutoff.

findings.summary: release_ok() checks truthiness rather than evidence from real controls.
findings.evidence: Strings 'False' for pii_minimized/rbac/slice_metrics/input_limits still pass.
findings.pedagogical_impact: A release can pass while controls are absent.
findings.attack: A release can pass while controls are absent.
findings.defense: Checklists can prevent omissions.
findings.proposed_fix: Require exact schema plus links to test/artifact/hash/result for each item.

findings.summary: slice_metrics=True substitutes for a fairness assessment.
findings.evidence: No y_true, y_pred, group feature, support, metric definition or uncertainty is computed.
findings.pedagogical_impact: 'We have slice metrics' can be mistaken for measured fairness evidence.
findings.attack: 'We have slice metrics' can be mistaken for measured fairness evidence.
findings.defense: S35 introduced fairness concepts.
findings.proposed_fix: Require a disaggregated metric artifact with support and uncertainty on the same eval set.

findings.summary: The prose uses 'false-queue rate' without numerator, denominator or ground truth.
findings.evidence: T3-A calls for slice metrics de false-queue rate.
findings.pedagogical_impact: Different teams can compute incompatible quantities under the same name.
findings.attack: Different teams can compute incompatible quantities under the same name.
findings.defense: The phrase is intuitively suggestive.
findings.proposed_fix: Define event, reference label and denominator explicitly.

findings.summary: SSRF prevention is a release requirement in prose but no URL validation/allowlist/network boundary exists.
findings.evidence: risk_checklist.py checks only input_limits=True.
findings.pedagogical_impact: Security is reduced to a checkbox.
findings.attack: Security is reduced to a checkbox.
findings.defense: The prose correctly identifies SSRF risk.
findings.proposed_fix: Implement a local URL-policy/allowlist fixture and tests, or explicitly defer remote fetching.

findings.summary: The prose says the risk owner signs the checklist, but no owner/reviewer ID, timestamp or reviewed hash is stored.
findings.evidence: release_ok() returns only a boolean.
findings.pedagogical_impact: External review cannot know who approved which version.
findings.attack: External review cannot know who approved which version.
findings.defense: Crypto signing is unnecessary for this lesson.
findings.proposed_fix: Persist approver_id, artifact hash, timestamp and decision.

findings.summary: mode() receives drift_high as an external boolean with no reference, metric, threshold or window.
findings.evidence: No drift statistic is computed.
findings.pedagogical_impact: The capstone can claim monitoring without monitoring evidence.
findings.attack: The capstone can claim monitoring without monitoring evidence.
findings.defense: Separating detection from policy can be good design.
findings.proposed_fix: Require a drift-event artifact with method/reference/current snapshot/metric/threshold/value/time.

findings.summary: The prose treats a spike in mean score as a calibration alert.
findings.evidence: T3-B says un pico de score medio ... dispara alerta de calibración.
findings.pedagogical_impact: Score-distribution shift does not establish calibration error without outcomes.
findings.attack: Score-distribution shift does not establish calibration error without outcomes.
findings.defense: A score shift is a useful alert.
findings.proposed_fix: Call it score/data drift unless labels support a calibration metric.

findings.summary: human_only is a returned mode string, not a policy that blocks automatic scoring/routing/actions.
findings.evidence: mode(False, True) returns human_only only.
findings.pedagogical_impact: The strongest safety mode can be claimed without changing behavior.
findings.attack: The strongest safety mode can be claimed without changing behavior.
findings.defense: A mode function is a clean abstraction.
findings.proposed_fix: Apply mode to the actual decision path and test forbidden automatic actions are blocked.

findings.summary: The outcome promises rollback of model/threshold, but code handles only a previous model ID.
findings.evidence: No threshold/calibrator/feature/reference/policy version is reverted.
findings.pedagogical_impact: Partial rollback can leave an inconsistent system.
findings.attack: Partial rollback can leave an inconsistent system.
findings.defense: Model rollback is the most visible example.
findings.proposed_fix: Rollback a compatibility-checked release bundle.

findings.summary: Any nonempty previous model string is accepted as rollback target.
findings.evidence: rollback_target('does-not-exist') returns it.
findings.pedagogical_impact: Runbook can point to a nonexistent/incompatible artifact.
findings.attack: Runbook can point to a nonexistent/incompatible artifact.
findings.defense: The helper is illustrative.
findings.proposed_fix: Resolve target in registry and verify availability/checksum/compatibility.

findings.summary: acceptance_bundle() lists six criterion names but executes none.
findings.evidence: n_criteria=6 comes from a list of strings.
findings.pedagogical_impact: The capstone can look ready without any passing test.
findings.attack: The capstone can look ready without any passing test.
findings.defense: Listing criteria is useful orientation.
findings.proposed_fix: Store command/test ID, result, artifact hash and failure details per criterion.

findings.summary: happy/override/ood_abstain are strings, not scenario runs.
findings.evidence: demo_paths is a static list.
findings.pedagogical_impact: Coverage can be claimed without proof.
findings.attack: Coverage can be claimed without proof.
findings.defense: The scenarios are correctly chosen.
findings.proposed_fix: Create fixtures and persist expected/observed outputs plus test results.

findings.summary: regression_smoke_s27_s39 is a name, not an executed regression.
findings.evidence: No pytest run/result manifest is attached.
findings.pedagogical_impact: CF-3 can appear ready while upstream P1 debt remains.
findings.attack: CF-3 can appear ready while upstream P1 debt remains.
findings.defense: A full retrain is unnecessary for every smoke.
findings.proposed_fix: Run critical contract/E2E/privacy tests and persist command/commit/environment/results.

findings.summary: The dossier omits roadmap-required version/revision, date, responsible owner, reviewer, paths/hashes, commands, results and issues.
findings.evidence: acceptance_bundle stores only cf3_review='external' and self_declared_promotion=False.
findings.pedagogical_impact: The checkpoint is not reconstructible.
findings.attack: The checkpoint is not reconstructible.
findings.defense: The prose avoids self-promotion correctly.
findings.proposed_fix: Implement a CF3Manifest matching the roadmap gate fields.

findings.summary: CP-N3-A/B/C are named but not linked to concrete versions/hashes/results.
findings.evidence: Reference prose says it receives A/B/C; no immutable refs exist.
findings.pedagogical_impact: S39 can integrate stale or imaginary capstones.
findings.attack: S39 can integrate stale or imaginary capstones.
findings.defense: Prior sections should have created them.
findings.proposed_fix: Require immutable artifact refs and gate results for all three.

findings.summary: cf3_review='external' does not prove an external review occurred.
findings.evidence: The string is hard-coded.
findings.pedagogical_impact: The anti-self-promotion safeguard is itself self-declared.
findings.attack: The anti-self-promotion safeguard is itself self-declared.
findings.defense: The prose explicitly says not to self-declare.
findings.proposed_fix: Keep review pending until reviewer ID, timestamp, reviewed hashes and decision exist.

findings.summary: T4-B creates card_types=['model','data','system'] rather than actual card artifacts.
findings.evidence: No card content, owner, version, metrics or limitations are persisted.
findings.pedagogical_impact: Documentation governance becomes a list of names.
findings.attack: Documentation governance becomes a list of names.
findings.defense: The prose gives a useful outline.
findings.proposed_fix: Create three versioned cards and validate required sections plus artifact links.

findings.summary: value_metrics() checks only key presence and accepts impossible values.
findings.evidence: Runtime accepts precision_at_k=2.5, override_rate=-1, median_review_s=NaN.
findings.pedagogical_impact: Invalid operational metrics can close the level.
findings.attack: Invalid operational metrics can close the level.
findings.defense: Presence checks are concise scaffolding.
findings.proposed_fix: Validate domains, finiteness, denominators/windows and provenance.

findings.summary: precision_at_k=0.55 is hand-entered with no ranked IDs, labels, k, tie policy or review coverage.
findings.evidence: T4-B stores only a scalar.
findings.pedagogical_impact: S36's P@k defects are carried forward.
findings.attack: S36's P@k defects are carried forward.
findings.defense: P@k is appropriate for ranked queues.
findings.proposed_fix: Compute it from versioned ranking/labels and record k/ties/coverage/window.

findings.summary: postmortem_ok() checks blameless=True plus nonempty root_cause/actions and ignores timeline/evidence/action ownership.
findings.evidence: Runtime accepts root_cause='person_x' and actions=[''].
findings.pedagogical_impact: A blameful or empty-action postmortem can pass.
findings.attack: A blameful or empty-action postmortem can pass.
findings.defense: A tiny validator cannot ensure writing quality.
findings.proposed_fix: Validate timeline, evidence-linked factors, nonempty actions with owner/due date and forbid person-as-root-cause patterns.

findings.summary: The example labels 'calib_drift' as root_cause although drift is usually a detected condition, not necessarily the causal process failure.
findings.evidence: postmortem['root_cause']='calib_drift'.
findings.pedagogical_impact: Learners may stop causal analysis at the monitoring signal.
findings.attack: Learners may stop causal analysis at the monitoring signal.
findings.defense: Calibration drift can directly contribute to bad decisions.
findings.proposed_fix: Call drift a contributing condition unless a causal mechanism is evidenced.

findings.summary: S39 has no collected pytest evidence for its critical integrator claims.
findings.evidence: Theory snippets print/return booleans; roadmap requires systematic pytest since S27.
findings.pedagogical_impact: None of the false greens blocks CI.
findings.attack: None of the false greens blocks CI.
findings.defense: Small snippets are readable.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a level-regression pytest suite and persist its run manifest.

findings.summary: The current Theory playground for integrator-phase2 is still CI/CD and monitoring.
findings.evidence: SectionView title is 'Practica CI/CD y monitoreo' with lint/test/build/deploy_canary.
findings.pedagogical_impact: Learners practice a different production topic after the N3 triage lesson.
findings.attack: Learners practice a different production topic after the N3 triage lesson.
findings.defense: CI/CD/monitoring are adjacent concepts.
findings.proposed_fix: Keep the stable ID but replace only the playground mapping with N3 triage/CF-3 evidence practice.

findings.summary: Responsible-AI controls collapse into one boolean checklist.
findings.evidence: release_ok() returns all([...]).
findings.pedagogical_impact: This promotes checkbox compliance at the integrator section.
findings.attack: This promotes checkbox compliance at the integrator section.
findings.defense: Checklists can prevent omissions.
findings.proposed_fix: Keep checklist as index but link each item to continuous GOVERN/MAP/MEASURE/MANAGE evidence.

findings.summary: The opening implies degradation from world change is detected by comparing today's inputs with validation inputs.
findings.evidence: It says drift se detecta comparando lo que entra hoy con lo que entraba cuando se validó.
findings.pedagogical_impact: Input drift may not imply performance drift, and concept/performance drift can occur without obvious input shift.
findings.attack: Input drift may not imply performance drift, and concept/performance drift can occur without obvious input shift.
findings.defense: Input comparison is one important signal.
findings.proposed_fix: Name it input/data drift and distinguish outcome-dependent drift/performance checks.

findings.summary: The opening says fairness 'es una métrica'.
findings.evidence: Fairness assessment is harm/context-specific and commonly uses multiple disaggregated metrics/supports.
findings.pedagogical_impact: Learners may look for one universal fairness number.
findings.attack: Learners may look for one universal fairness number.
findings.defense: By-group monitoring is directionally good.
findings.proposed_fix: Say fairness is a recurring assessment using selected harm-relevant metrics, support and uncertainty.

findings.summary: risk_checklist contains auto_fraud=False, but release_ok() ignores it.
findings.evidence: Setting auto_fraud=True leaves release_ok unchanged when five checked fields pass.
findings.pedagogical_impact: The central no-autofraud safeguard can be violated while release_ok=True.
findings.attack: The central no-autofraud safeguard can be violated while release_ok=True.
findings.defense: Other prose repeats the safety boundary.

findings.summary: The six acceptance criteria omit explicit privacy, fairness, no-leakage, durable-resilience and upstream capstone gate evidence.
findings.evidence: Criteria are e2e, baseline, abstention, audit log, no_auto_fraud_label, regression smoke.
findings.pedagogical_impact: A nominal acceptance bundle can omit controls required by CF-3/N3 regression.
findings.attack: A nominal acceptance bundle can omit controls required by CF-3/N3 regression.
findings.defense: Some could be intended inside regression_smoke.
findings.proposed_fix: Expand the manifest or require regression results to enumerate these controls explicitly.

USABLE: Score prioritization can be separated from fraud/guilt verdicts.
Calibration and operational threshold selection are distinct decisions.
Evidence packets should expose facts/path/explanation rather than score alone.
Human override and appeal are legitimate governance mechanisms when audited.
Input/data drift is a useful operational signal but not a moral verdict.
Incident > drift > normal is a defensible safety-priority ordering.
Model/data/system cards are useful documentation categories.
External review rather than self-declared promotion is the correct CF-3 governance principle.
PARTIAL: End-to-end stage integration and contract versioning.
Audit log, override, appeal and feedback.
